name: Lin Zhibin
profile: Lin Zhibin is chairman of Xiamen-based Ruida Futures, a futures brokerage incorporated in 1993 and the first futures company listed on the Shenzhen market. Together with Lin Hongbin and Lin Lifang he controls the company as an acting-in-concert party through Ruida Holdings, per the 2024 annual report.
interesting_fact: Ruida Futures was the first listed futures brokerage on the Shenzhen market and the first Fujian futures firm to win a financial-futures brokerage licence.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he was named 'Best Helmsman of a Chinese Futures Company' (中国期货公司最佳掌舵人) at the 10th China Best Futures Operating Institutions awards.
notes: No personal channels found; reach via company IR (SZSE 002961) website. Personal biography (age, education) not found in accessible sources.

name: Guo Huabin
current_role: Chairman, Jiangxi Yaosheng Industry and Trade Development Co., Ltd. (Yaosheng Tungsten), per Asian Metal Jan 2024
profile: Guo Huabin heads Jiangxi Yaosheng, a private Ganzhou-region tungsten group listed by Hurun under tungsten mining, tourism and hotels. Asian Metal describes the company as running a full tungsten chain from mining and beneficiation to smelting, powder and cemented carbide production and trading.
interesting_fact: Yaosheng's stated annual capacities include 3,000t tungsten concentrate, 9,000t APT, 6,000t tungsten oxide, 4,000t tungsten powder and 2,500t tungsten carbide powder.
deep_cut_fact: In a January 2024 meeting with Asian Metal he discussed problems in tin mine production and smelting, showing Yaosheng's interest beyond tungsten into tin.
notes: Titled President in June 2023 and Chairman in Jan 2024 Asian Metal visit reports. Very low public profile; no personal or press contacts found. Trade-press (Asian Metal) is the main English-language footprint.

name: Liu Changjei
current_role: Founder and former chairman/GM of Shandong Longquan Pipeline Engineering (SZSE: 002671); current role not confirmed
profile: Liu Changjie (刘长杰, b. March 1959) led a group of 26 founders who set up Zibo Longquan Pipeline Engineering in 2000, making prestressed concrete cylinder pipe (PCCP) for water-diversion projects; it listed in Shenzhen in 2012 with him as controlling shareholder (41.4%). Control of the company later passed to Guangdong Jianhua.
interesting_fact: Longquan's PCCP pipes were used in major water projects such as Beijing's Zhangfang diversion, Suzhou's Taihu diversion and Liaoning's Dahuofang reservoir transfer (phase II).
deep_cut_fact: He rose through Zibo Cement Products Factory as office director, assistant to the director, deputy director and then director, and was named one of Shandong's 'Meritorious Entrepreneurs of 30 Years of Reform and Opening' in building materials (2009).
notes: Hurun lists him under 'Longquan / Cement'; matched to Shandong Longquan Pipeline (concrete pipe) via 2012 prospectus. Name likely 'Liu Changjie'. Later filings show Guangdong Jianhua as controlling shareholder; his current involvement not verified.

name: Wang Yinglin
current_role: General Manager and Director, Shanghai SK Automation Technology Co., Ltd. (SSE STAR: 688155)
profile: Wang Yinglin has been general manager and a director of Shanghai SK Automation (先惠技术) since its founding in 2007, and holds roughly a fifth of its shares per data aggregators. The Shanghai company makes intelligent manufacturing equipment such as EV battery-module/pack lines and chassis and engine assembly lines.
interesting_fact: A MarketScreener headline reports SK Automation landing a '106 Million' deal with battery giant CATL.
notes: Aggregators disagree on gender/age; no personal biography found. Chairman/CTO is Pan Yanqing. Best route is via company investor relations (688155).

name: Liu Danying
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party of the controlling shareholder, Xi'an Tianhe Defense Technology (SZSE: 300397)
profile: Liu Danying is the wife and acting-in-concert partner of He Zenglin, controlling shareholder of Xi'an Tianhe Defense Technology, a defense electronics maker. A Sept 2024 filing shows she held 3.04% directly (28.15% combined with He) and is a limited partner (10%) in Xi'an Junyao Linghang, the vehicle used for a private placement.
interesting_fact: In the 2024 private placement, the subscriber Xi'an Junyao Linghang was 90% funded by He Zenglin as general partner and 10% by Liu Danying as limited partner.
notes: Wealth shared with husband He Zenglin; she appears in filings only as a shareholder. No biography or contacts found; any approach should go via Tianhe Defense IR / He Zenglin.

name: Zhang Ye
current_role: Co-founder and (as of 2016) chairman & CEO of Yiguo; chairman of eTrade/Yimao Holdings (易贸控股); current status not verified
profile: Zhang Ye co-founded Yiguo, one of China's earliest fresh-produce e-commerce platforms, in 2005 with Jin Guanglei and Mao Lu, after building Shanghai-based Yimao (founded 1999), a B2B commodity information and trading platform for chemicals, energy and pulp & paper. He studied at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
interesting_fact: Yiguo began in 2005 when the founders asked whether consumers could buy quality imported fruit online at fair prices; co-founder Mao Lu was then doing customs clearance for imported fruit.
deep_cut_fact: He earned two bachelor's degrees at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, in industrial foreign trade and in computing; colleagues say his palate is weak, so co-founder Jin Guanglei spots over-seasoned dishes. His line: 'In the future there is no e-commerce, only fresh food.'
notes: Very low-profile; a 2016 TMTPost profile said almost no public information on him existed. Yiguo's current state not verified in this pass; check before outreach. Yimao (eTrade) Holdings is the likely current route.

name: Xiong Liwu
current_role: Major shareholder of Wuhu Bethel Automotive Safety Systems (SSE: 603596); executive role not confirmed
profile: Xiong Liwu appears as a large individual shareholder of Bethel (伯特利), a Wuhu-based automotive brake and safety-systems supplier in which Chery is also a major shareholder. A reported reduction plan cited a 12.87% stake; a March 2026 shareholder list shows 1.85%.
notes: Name matched to Bethel shareholder lists (usmart.hk, sohu); no biography found, so link to Hurun entry is probable but not confirmed. Has been selling down; no contacts found.

name: Mu Qiru
current_role: Chairperson and actual controller, Beijing Zhaotai Group (兆泰集团)
profile: Mu Qiru (b. 1951) founded Beijing Zhaotai Group in the early 1990s (1992 per its site); it develops and operates offices, mixed-use and commercial property (e.g. Fenghui Times Building, Dinghao Electronics Building) plus health, retail and energy investments. She holds 69.15% and 80.7% of voting rights; in late 2023 she hired Han Shi, the executive behind Joy City.
interesting_fact: Zhaotai is redeveloping the Dinghao Electronics Building in Zhongguancun as an urban-renewal project run by its Fenghui Space light-asset platform.
deep_cut_fact: As a young woman she worked as a horse herder in Dong Ujimqin Banner, Inner Mongolia, then taught primary school in Beijing, and in the 1980s helped found Beijing Youth Travel Service, rising to deputy GM before starting Zhaotai.
notes: Zhaotai Group's own website not verified in this pass. Low-profile; route via Zhaotai corporate office.

name: Wu Jiang
current_role: Deceased; former chairman of Zhejiang Zomax Transmission (中马传动, SSE: 603767)
profile: Wu Jiang, second-generation chairman of Zomax Transmission from 2012, died of illness in February 2023 aged 55, per Jiemian (12 Dec 2023). Control then passed to his father, founder Wu Liangxing, and his widow.

name: Baijnath Choudhary
current_role: Founder of Anmol Industries (Anmol Biscuits), Kolkata; promoter via Baijnath Choudhary & Family Trust
profile: Baijnath Choudhary founded Kolkata-based Anmol Industries, a maker of biscuits, cookies and cakes that traces its origins to 1994 and a first plant at Dankuni, West Bengal. It now runs seven plants in UP, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha. In Sept 2026 it filed for a Rs 1,800 crore IPO, entirely an offer for sale by the Baijnath Choudhary & Family Trust.
interesting_fact: As of March 2026 Anmol had capacity of about 361,000 tonnes a year of biscuits and cookies; family packs alone brought Rs 485.5 crore of FY2026 product sales.
deep_cut_fact: Anmol's first manufacturing plant was at Dankuni, West Bengal; the company says its founder came from humble beginnings and put strong emphasis on philanthropy.
notes: Day-to-day leadership appears to be with other Choudhary family members (e.g. a 2014 interview names Gobind Ram Choudhary as MD). Whether the founder is living was not confirmed. IPO DRHP (Sept 2026) would list company IR contacts.

name: Shangguan Wenlong
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Guangzhou Sanfu New Materials Technology (SSE STAR: 688359)
profile: Shangguan Wenlong is the controlling shareholder and, with Qu Chenghong, actual controller of Guangzhou Sanfu New Materials Technology, a specialty chemicals maker listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2021. A Sept 2024 filing records a reduction of his stake via a negotiated transfer.
interesting_fact: Sanfu returned to profit in H1 2026, with revenue up about 50% to 341 million yuan.
notes: No biography found in accessible sources; check the 2021 STAR prospectus for background. Approach via company IR (688359).

name: Wang Dan
current_role: Shareholder (8.49% direct) and acting-in-concert party of Shanghai Shunho New Materials (SZSE: 002565); former actual controller
profile: Wang Dan, a Hong Kong-registered Chinese national, was long the actual controller (with Zhang Shaohuai) of Shanghai Shunho, a packaging/printing company whose main customers include state and foreign tobacco firms. In 2019 he transferred Shunho Investment Group to his son Wang Zhenglin, who became actual controller from 1 Jan 2023 when a voting-proxy arrangement expired.
interesting_fact: Control passed to the next generation via a staged handover: equity moved in Nov 2019, but Wang Dan kept the voting rights under a proxy until it expired at end-2022.
notes: Succession done; son Wang Zhenglin is now actual controller and legal representative, so he may be the better contact. No personal biography found.

name: Tony Brotherton-Ratcliffe
current_role: Retired (2020) Non-Executive Chairman of Croudace Homes Group; family owners of Croudace
profile: Tony Brotherton-Ratcliffe is the son of Jack Brotherton-Ratcliffe, who co-founded South-East housebuilder Croudace in 1946 and owned it outright from 1957. Tony became non-executive chairman in 2001 when his father retired at 81, and retired in 2020, handing over to his nephew Caspar Brotherton. The family's wealth (shared with Diana Jones in the Rich List) comes from Croudace.
interesting_fact: Croudace's first private development (Haroldslea Close, Horley, 1951) bought land at £100 per house; two-bed homes sold for £1,690.
deep_cut_fact: Croudace began in 1946 repairing bomb-damaged properties after WWII, and its first new-build contract (1947) was 200 council houses in Bletchingley, Surrey; in 1962 it won consent for Vigo Village, an 800-home New Town-style scheme on a former army camp in Kent.
notes: Private family; retired from the board in 2020. Estates Gazette rich lists also cite the family via Croudace. Best route is via Croudace Homes Group head office.
